◘«Saint Stylianos of Paphlagonia» – 26 November

◘In these days, when we are living history with emotion, I am showing you the icon of «Saint Stylianos», painted in our workshop for a holy church in Dobrogea.

◘«Saint Stylianos», one of the saints closest to children, was a hermit monk from the province of Paphlagonia, canonised as a saint. He is considered the patron saint of children and of the Christian family. His life of prayer and his love of God made him worthy of the gift of working miracles, especially healing sick children. In the calendar of saints, his feast day is 26 November.

◘Happy name day to all who celebrate!

4f472193d9fb:
The Burning Bush – icon painted on glass

"The Burning Bush is the symbol of unceasing prayer: whoever prays unceasingly is like this bush that burned and was not consumed. We are always under the fire of God – this blaze of light and power – and the more it burns, the brighter we become and the closer to God. That is one meaning of the Burning Bush."
Father Sofian Boghiu

Under the name “The Burning Bush of the Mother of God”, a Christian and cultural society was active at the Antim Monastery in Bucharest (between 1946 and 1948) which regarded prayer as one of the paths to salvation. The initiator and driving force of this society was the poet and journalist Sandu Tudor, who became a monk under the name Daniil. Together with a group of lay intellectuals and monks (a group that wished to preserve the true Orthodox faith and Orthodox values in times of atheist communism), he founded a Christian and cultural society that regarded prayer as one of the paths to salvation. The association's name was “The Burning Bush” – the bush which, according to the Bible, burns with an ever-green flame and which symbolises the union of the saved soul with the absolute. Sandu Tudor brought an old icon from Mount Athos dedicated to the Burning Bush, an icon from which I dared to take inspiration in painting the icon I am showing you today. The icon is not available; I will paint it again only to order.

00f1103bba43:
The Baptism of the Lord Jesus Christ – icon painted on glass

The theme of this icon (the most recent icon I have painted on this theme) is the Baptism of the Lord.
The Sacrament of Holy Baptism is the sacrament of being born again, the sacrament of a person's spiritual birth. Through biological or bodily birth, man is born for this earthly life and goes towards death because of ancestral sin, which has been passed on to all people as a predisposition or inclination to sin. So whoever is born physically in Adam, as a human being, is born to die physically; but whoever is born spiritually in Christ, through Baptism with water and the Holy Spirit, is born to live forever, according to the Saviour's words: “Whoever believes in Me, though he die, yet shall he live”.

The Baptism of the Lord Jesus Christ (Theophany) is celebrated today, 6 January.

In the depiction of the Baptism in this icon (model: Șcheii Brașovului, first half of the 19th century)
Jesus is in the middle, standing in the waters of the Jordan; on His right is John the Baptist, and on His left the angel holding the cloth. Above, the Holy Spirit is shown in the form of a dove.
91c852899c0b:
The Baptism of the Lord Jesus Christ – icon painted on glass

The theme of the Baptism of the Lord, one of the great events of Christendom, also called Theophany, Epiphany or the Divine Manifestation, holds an important place in the peasant icons on glass.
The icon (painted after a model from Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century) shows Jesus Christ in a humble attitude, with His hands crossed on His chest, at the moment He is baptised by His Forerunner, the great prophet John. Also in a humble attitude is an angel of the Lord, holding a towel in both hands as the Lord comes out of the waters of the Jordan.)

The icon is painted on glass in several layers, using tempera and gold leaf, over a pen-and-ink drawing made after the original model.
The ink drawing is fixed and protected with varnish, and the finished painting has a protective layer of colour with linseed oil.
The stained fir frame is also handmade.
Icon size: 21x29 cm (without frame); 27.55x35.5 cm (with frame)

Epiphany, or Theophany (from the Greek theophania, meaning “the appearance / manifestation of God”), is one of the Great Feasts of the Orthodox Church, celebrated on 6 January.
On this day we celebrate the baptism of the Lord Jesus Christ by Saint John the Baptist in the river Jordan and the beginning of Christ's early preaching. The feast of Epiphany marks the end of the Christmas celebrations, which begin on 25 December and end on 6 January. During the service of this feast, the Great Blessing of the Waters takes place; the holy water is used by priests to bless the homes of the faithful.

The feast is called Theophany because at the baptism of Christ the Holy Trinity appeared to the world for the first time: the voice of the Father is heard from heaven, the Son is incarnate and stands in the river Jordan, and the Holy Spirit descends upon Him in the form of a dove.

The icon is not available; it will be painted again to order!
